central_topic: Reliability and reference-measure efficiency of training-only locally scaled split-conformal regions for continuous logistic-normal compositions in isometric log-ratio coordinates, evaluated across homoscedastic, boundary-concentrated heteroscedastic, and covariate-shift settings.
core_methods: Split conformal prediction with finite-sample corrected calibration ranks and positive covariate-dependent residual normalization
Isometric log-ratio (ILR) representation with a shared training-only ridge-regression center
Quadratic-feature ridge regression of log residual norms as the incumbent scale model
Additive quantile-regression stumps targeting the 0.9 quantile of log residual norms with pinball loss
Training-only three-fold selection among ridge, constant, and log-space ridge/tail blends using fitting-only quantile alignment and a one-standard-error heuristic
comparators: Unscaled global ILR split-conformal residual-norm regions
Raw-simplex L-infinity split-conformal regions and coordinatewise Bonferroni regions
Uncalibrated training-residual quantiles, full-simplex regions, and singleton-center sanity baselines
Conformalized quantile regression as related quantile-based methodology, not an implemented baseline or an equivalent region construction
Covariate-shift-aware conformal inference as theoretical context, not a weighted method implemented in this run
Limits of distribution-free conditional coverage for interpreting empirical subgroup diagnostics
benchmarks: Task-owned logistic-normal-v1 synthetic continuous compositions with six covariates and dimensions 3 and 10; no real dataset was evaluated
H3 and H10: interior homoscedastic responses
B3 and B10: boundary-concentrated heteroscedastic responses, still strictly positive rather than exact-zero compositions
S3 and S10: boundary-concentrated heteroscedastic responses with a test-covariate mean shift

Final evaluation: six independent seed episodes, nominal coverage levels 0.95 and 0.90, fixed groups defined by the sign of the first covariate, Wilson intervals, and paired seed-bootstrap utility intervals
architectural_shifts: Scale-model comparison: quadratic-feature log-norm ridge versus a training-selected family that adds quantile stumps and log-space blends; aggregate results do not identify which component caused the difference

Region-representation comparison: raw-simplex L-infinity and coordinatewise regions versus global and locally scaled Euclidean residual-norm regions in ILR coordinates; the center remains shared and fixed
No neural architecture, pretrained model, or cross-dataset transfer is evidenced; the interaction-tree extension has no successful evaluation
result_driven_themes: The strongest successful search configuration is the tail-adaptive selection family; its small aggregate advantage over the incumbent is not an isolated quantile-stump effect or a demonstrated statistically significant between-configuration gain

Final aggregate utility exceeds global ILR and constant/permuted controls with positive paired seed-bootstrap intervals; this supports studying covariate-dependent scaling within these synthetic workloads, not universal superiority
Case-level final means show larger gains over global ILR in B/S settings and slightly lower utility in H settings, motivating heteroscedasticity-specific rather than uniform-benefit framing

Empirical marginal and fixed-group coverage errors must be separated from finite-sample marginal validity; ordinary split-conformal guarantees do not automatically extend to the shifted S cases or conditional coverage
Efficiency is reference probability mass under a mixture of training-derived ILR Gaussian probes and uniform-simplex probes, not geometric simplex volume

queries.rationale: Foundational anchor supplied in the starter literature for split-conformal calibration and locally adaptive regression. The implemented method uses training-only positive residual scales and evaluator-owned corrected calibration ranks; this query covers the validity/scaling foundation without a risky direct search for conformal composition evaluation.

queries.query: quantile regression boosting decision stumps pinball loss
queries.rationale: The successful implementation fits additive quantile stumps to log residual norms at quantile 0.9 and selects ridge/tail blends on training folds. Retrieve the quantile-loss and boosting lineage, not unsupported interaction forests; aggregate evidence cannot attribute gains to stumps alone.

A natural neighboring literature when learning a residual-tail quantile for conformal inference. Explain the distinction: this run learns a single positive scale for an ILR norm region, not lower/upper response quantiles, and did not evaluate CQR as a baseline.

queries.query: "Isometric logratio transformations for compositional data analysis"
queries.rationale: The actual representation comparison is raw-simplex coordinate regions versus Euclidean residual norms in an ILR basis with a shared ridge center. Foundational ILR geometry explains the representation without suggesting a neural architectural transition.

queries.query: logistic normal distribution compositional data simplex
queries.rationale: All evaluated responses come from the task-owned continuous logistic-normal generator in dimensions 3 and 10. Establish distributional context and distinguish near-boundary positive compositions from multinomial counts, latent-target reconstruction, and exact zeros; internal H/B/S labels are not external benchmark names.

The evaluator includes raw-coordinate L-infinity regions and coordinatewise Bonferroni regions, alongside global ILR norm regions. Retrieve multivariate joint-coverage and coordinatewise comparison literature; do not present a geometry-specific efficiency ranking independent of the chosen reference measure.

The S3/S10 workloads explicitly shift test covariates and show aggregate utility gains from local scaling. This supplied starter reference is needed to delimit exchangeability-based claims and distinguish empirical shifted-distribution performance from weighted-conformal validity; weighting was not implemented.

queries.query: limits distribution free conditional predictive inference conditional coverage
queries.rationale: The final evaluator reports both marginal and sign-of-first-covariate group coverage errors. Search the conditional-coverage limitation literature to avoid upgrading fixed-group empirical diagnostics or positive aggregate utility gaps into conditional, multivalid, or subgroup coverage guarantees.
